purpose: Test the feasibility of mathematical signal/noise analysis on openly published physical photodiode recordings, without falsely treating legacy records as prospective results of JANUS LIGHT-008.

source.source_description: ESP32 two-pixel event vision sensor; photodiodes and LM324 analog signal conditioning; three separate publicly described tests: no-light, full-light and alternating motion.
source.project_license_statement: No repository license detected at time of audit. No third-party raw data are reproduced in this artifact; only source links and numeric summaries are retained.
source.source_units: t_ms: relative logged milliseconds, VA/VB: analog channel voltage; spA_s and spB_s: event-rate fields. Not photon time-tag records.

methods.parse: Read all numeric rows in each pinned CSV; preserve original ordering, do not filter rows or treat conditions as paired randomized trials.
methods.summary: Arithmetic sample mean and sample standard deviation (ddof=1) for channel A and B, plus mean and sample SD of adjacent t_ms differences.
methods.contrast: Full-light mean minus no-light mean per channel. Physical sensor output contrast is observational, not a controlled effect-size estimate with independent replication.
methods.forecast_demonstration: Within EACH separate condition, use first 16 points to estimate a constant training-mean predictor for VA, then score last 17 against constant train-mean and one-step persistence (previous observed VA). Both are simplistic baselines; not a fitted JANUS Ocean model.
methods.errors: Mean absolute error in raw volts on each 17-row holdout, calculated without removing samples.
methods.no_retraining_or_hyperparameter_search_a: Baseline formulas were chosen for this retrospective feasibility calculation, not before original public collection.

computed_contrasts.note: Different physical recording sessions; the contrast may include uncontrolled offsets and conditions.

conclusions: Public raw recordings suffice for concrete numerical photodiode signal/noise and baseline-forecast calculations without running the user's own ESP32.
Two independent analog channels show a roughly 0.28-V mean shift between full-light and no-light published sessions.
Both stationary conditions have small ~1–1.5 mV sample standard deviation, but one-second sample rate cannot resolve small photon flight times.
Across the two separate, short 17-point holdouts, a constant training mean has lower MAE than naive one-step persistence; no superior JANUS model has yet been evaluated.
These data do not match the preregistered LIGHT-008 requirement of 256 calibration and 256 test observations at 50-ms bins with an independently witnessed precommit.
No independently randomized later free-choice intervention or photon time-tagging is recorded here. No retrocausality inference is supported.

future_gate.conditions: Choose and pin a larger open physical time-series dataset before examining its test labels; fix cutoff, model and baselines; log independent dataset acquisition date and checksum; report gains AND losses. Retrospective publication cannot be a prospective time experiment.
